english: A basket contains 4 identical apples, 2 identical bananas and 5 mangoes of five different varieties. Consider all possible selections of fruits from the basket, the empty selection included; two selections are different if they differ in the number of apples, the number of bananas or the set of mangoes chosen. Then the arithmetic mean of the number of fruits in a selection, taken over all these selections, is ______.
hindi: एक टोकरी में 4 सर्वसम सेब, 2 सर्वसम केले तथा पाँच भिन्न किस्मों के 5 आम हैं। टोकरी से फलों के सभी सम्भव चयनों पर विचार कीजिए, जिसमें रिक्त चयन भी सम्मिलित है; दो चयन भिन्न माने जाते हैं यदि उनमें सेबों की संख्या, केलों की संख्या अथवा चुने गए आमों का समुच्चय भिन्न हो। तब इन सभी चयनों पर लिए गए, एक चयन में फलों की संख्या का समान्तर माध्य ______ है।
solution: Selections: apples $0..4$ (5 ways), bananas $0..2$ (3 ways), mangoes any subset ($2^{5}$): total $5\cdot3\cdot32=480$
The three choices are independent, so mean size $=$ mean apples $+$ mean bananas $+$ mean mangoes
solution_full: A selection is given by the number $a\in\{0,\ldots,4\}$ of apples, the number $b\in\{0,1,2\}$ of bananas and a subset $M$ of the 5 mangoes. Hence there are $5\cdot3\cdot2^{5}=480$ selections (including the empty one; $479$ non-empty, the $(p+1)(q+1)2^{n}-1$ count).

The size of a selection is $a+b+|M|$. Summing over all 480 selections, each value of $a$ occurs $3\cdot32=96$ times, so $\sum a=96(0+1+2+3+4)=960$; each value of $b$ occurs $5\cdot32=160$ times, so $\sum b=160(0+1+2)=480$.
For the mangoes, the number of subsets of size $k$ is $\binom{5}{k}$ and each is combined with $15$ choices of $(a,b)$: $\sum|M|=15\sum_{k=0}^{5}k\binom{5}{k}=15\cdot5\cdot2^{4}=1200$.
originality_note: New: the mean size of a selection from a mixed collection (identical apples, identical bananas, distinct mangoes) over all selections including the empty one, which separates into independent means because the count is a product (way 4: independence turns a long sum into three short ones). Closest known: 'number of selections from p alike, q alike and n distinct objects: (p+1)(q+1)2^n - 1'. Different because: the question asks for a weighted total over all selections, not their number.

concept_use.Selection from a mix of distinct and ide: Identical apples and bananas are selected by number only (5 and 3 choices).
